title: CLO3D PNG Export Issue
content:
Has anyone had issues with slow PNG exports from the Save Image function?

I am using the CLO3D Enterprise software and don't understand why the PNG export takes so long to save PNGs or even load views often. I've received feedback before that slow files may be due to too many colorways or complex patterns, but I think there are technical issues with how the software is even reading information...updating thumbnails, loading custom views for PNG export, or even loading color and textures.  
  
The logic / rationale doesn't make sense to me: 

  * The PNG export reloads views multiple separate times and can take very long to load colorways each time...first clicking the Save Image button, CLO3D takes a long time for the Creating Preview Images loading bar to finish before the Snapshot box opens; second, when the box loads and recreates thumbnails for the current views; and third...CLO3D will refresh the current view, reloading each colorway's thumbnails and THEN load the custom .mvs file and recreate thumbnails for each colorway.

  * From what I can infer based on how files save into folders, CLO3D is first exporting individual views…then saving the entire group view for all colorways...then going back across all colorways,  _reloading from the beginning_ the work that it had already exported, to get the group PNG image export...Please explain why this is the way the program exports images. I think this is creating bottlenecks in the system logic and adding exponentially to the time it takes to get work done. This has been an issue across multiple versions, for the Individual and Enterprise licenses, and seems like a fundamental flaw in how a designer can even show the work they have done with this software.  
  
I've linked a video of exporting a basic cube as a reference...but obviously with a more complex pattern and more colorways, all parts of the process start to lag significantly. I have checked that the hardware exceeds CLO3D's minimum requirements. I just don't understand this issue or why the program runs like this and would appreciate more insight.  
  


YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fMGAh6x_OYE

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Ricky, as an enterprise user, please reach out to your CLO representative directly. If you do not know who this is, let us know and they will contact you :)
content_description: To discuss and seek insights into the causes of slow PNG export and view loading performance issues in CLO3D software, particularly related to its handling of colorways, thumbnails, and export logic.

title: Meet the Winner: Creator's contest 2025 Vol.1 - Seifuku Decoded (3rd place, Kimura)
content:
## _Meet a seasoned pattern maker,_[_Kimura_](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/19750/collection/collections) _, with over 20 years of experience who’s now pushing the boundaries of digital fashion creation with Marvelous Designer and CLO.  
From futuristic uniforms to game-style texture work with CLO and Substance Painter—  
this inspiring interview dives deep into the creative process that bridges fashion and CG._

![b937555d9cf04661874f81a40519a968](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/b937555d9cf04661874f81a40519a9681.png)

# **Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

I’ve been working in the apparel industry for over 20 years as a pattern maker. While my main focus has been women's wear, I’ve also created patterns for menswear, sportswear, and stage costumes, and have been involved in planning rental wear and event merchandise.

In recent years, I’ve embraced digital tools such as CLO3D and Marvelous Designer to create 3D garment data. I’m also involved in advisory work related to the integration of apparel technology and AI, using my background as a technical expert to support early-stage planning and problem-solving.

I’ve expanded my activities into creative and educational fields as well, including producing promotional videos that combine CLO and Unreal Engine, and teaching short courses on CLO3D and Marvelous Designer.

The main reason I applied for this contest was actually the opportunity to receive a one-year Marvelous Designer license—I primarily use CLO3D in my daily work, so that perk was especially appealing.

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Creator’s contest 2025 Vol.1 Seifuku Decoded Contest. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

The first thing I thought about was choosing a shape or theme that others might not typically create.

I felt that having more diversity in the entries would make the contest more engaging for viewers and enhance the overall visual impact of the exhibition.

Since I assumed that many participants would focus on women's fashion, I decided to design something that could be worn as menswear or unisex.

I also anticipated that many entries might feature school uniforms or designs suited for teenagers, so I deliberately avoided that direction.

As a first step, I began by gathering reference materials.

I collected images of occupational uniforms, and even garments commonly worn in specific professions that aren’t strictly "uniforms," to explore various design ideas.

During this process, I realized that in addition to practical factors like visibility and mobility, uniforms often carry a sense of authority as well.

I began to see how uniform design evolves in response to the changing needs of its wearers.

That led me to decide on the theme: "What might uniforms look like in the near future?"

• With the advancement of personal devices, I imagined that people would carry fewer and smaller items.

So I designed the outfit to include practical, wearable storage and easily accessible pockets.

![84d344b100a048b390ca031a97a85ea2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/84d344b100a048b390ca031a97a85ea22.png)

• I also envisioned a growing demand for uniforms that are functional and comfortable in any environment.

Specifically:

① Weather-resistant yet breathable design that can handle rain and wind

② Detachable sleeves and vests to adapt to different seasons

![607076e95b5e456e84cb8f8547288987](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/607076e95b5e456e84cb8f85472889873.png)![dc3868f047b04b4a8c43687a57193497](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/dc3868f047b04b4a8c43687a571934974.png)

③ Generous ease in the fabric to allow for a wide range of motion

—for example, pants designed to allow the wearer to open their legs wide

![c97d28dd6fa34fac9b7e624100e3b38a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/c97d28dd6fa34fac9b7e624100e3b38a5.png)![8104bc6efaa44414a91791f754e779ba](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/8104bc6efaa44414a91791f754e779ba6.png)

• Although I made a few adjustments to optimize it for 3D presentation, the pattern is fully functional and could be used to produce an actual garment

![8d9249fedaf54a9596da10c596fdd1bb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/8d9249fedaf54a9596da10c596fdd1bb7.png)

For the color scheme, I incorporated cyberpunk-inspired elements to give it a futuristic feel.

To better highlight the garment’s construction, I chose an avatar without a face and used a clean, minimal background.

![e43f443e0da341be9455743da7476d39](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/e43f443e0da341be9455743da7476d398.png)

Since this is a CLO/Marvelous Designer contest, I wanted to make the most of the tools and submitted renderings created in CLO.

I thought it would be a great opportunity to showcase what’s possible within CLO.

# **Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

I started by creating the garment pattern using 2D CAD software.

Since I have experience as a pattern maker, this step isn’t usually a challenge as long as the design is finalized.

The one thing I paid particular attention to was making sure that the garment would not only look good as a 3D model, but also make structural sense as a real, wearable piece.

Once the pattern was complete, I exported the data as a DXF file, which can be imported into CLO.

Next, I brought the DXF file into CLO and assembled the garment.

During this stage, I made adjustments so that the final piece would appeal both to people with a background in fashion and to those in the CG or animation industries.

This included checking that the garment had realistic ease for movement, natural-looking wrinkles, and a three-dimensional structure that would create appealing shadows and highlights.

After finishing the construction, I did some quick color testing in CLO to explore different palettes.

I assigned different materials and colors to each part and separated them by UV areas—this approach made it easier for me to manage later.

![9aed718d04c846d89dafc01a1ddad850](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/9aed718d04c846d89dafc01a1ddad8509.png)![4fa3b38469cd41ccb7b88a46410c0390](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/4fa3b38469cd41ccb7b88a46410c039010.png)

For the texture work, I used Substance Painter.

I applied shading to show seam allowances and garment thickness, and for areas where heat bonding was assumed, I avoided adding thickness.

I also added stylized wear-and-tear effects such as dirt on edges, wrinkling, and fading—somewhat exaggerated, in the style often used in games.

As mentioned in the art direction section, I chose to render the final piece in CLO.

I applied the textures exported from Substance Painter to the CLO garment parts and fine-tuned elements like roughness to get the final look.

# **If you have any tips or techniques related to Marvelous Designer, please feel free to share them with the community!**

I think it's best to approach pattern making without overcomplicating it — keep it simple!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/fd19ffe98f984e068c3db6da29fb6b99%E1%84%86%E1%85%B5%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%84%87%E1%85%A9%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%20June%2026%202025%2014%3A34%3A03.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/d557e9ac987b4caca5c84cd3b792fb07/images/91849fc536d74dd893844a447ef6a389%E1%84%86%E1%85%B5%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%84%87%E1%85%A9%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%20June%2026%202025%2014%3A34%3A03.jpg)

title: Chilean Lingerie Designer Bringing Intimate Fashion to Life with CLO
content:
### 

## [_Beatriz Hermosilla_](https://www.instagram.com/bea3designer/) _is a lingerie and pattern designer from Chile with a passion for craftsmanship and a strong technical foundation. She recently embraced 3D design as a natural next step in her creative process. By using CLO, she blends traditional sewing skills with digital innovation to create expressive, high-detail virtual lingerie prototypes. In this interview, Beatriz shares her 3D journey, the power of digital tools for indie designers, and how she’s helping shape the future of intimate apparel in Latin America._

* * *

**Can you tell us a bit about yourself and how you got into lingerie design?**  


Hi, I'm Beatríz Hermosilla from Chile. I’m a fashion designer specializing in lingerie design and pattern making.

From the beginning of my career, I found intimate fashion to be a space for both technical and aesthetic exploration—something I’m deeply passionate about. Today, I work independently as a lingerie pattern designer and also teach sewing classes focused on lingerie, where I share the techniques and processes I’ve refined over the years.

In 2023, I decided to expand my skills into the digital realm, integrating 3D technology into my creative practice. This shift has allowed me to experiment with textile simulations, iterate patterns more efficiently, and develop virtual prototypes that elevate my lingerie work to a new level of creativity and precision.

![3d7986d8a1814a70ab435f1a6195cebb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/01956365227a4857b5a85bc21a36c38e/images/3d7986d8a1814a70ab435f1a6195cebbTURN_1%20%281%29.png)

**Tell us about the project you created in CLO. What inspired it?**

I decided to recreate a piece by Atelier Bordelle in 3D as a way to challenge and strengthen my technical skills with CLO. I chose this design specifically for its structural complexity—it presented the perfect opportunity to dive deeper into 3D modeling and achieve a highly detailed finish.

Throughout the process, I carefully analyzed every component of the original garment, translating it into precise digital patterns and testing different materials and construction techniques in CLO. The goal was to achieve a realistic and visually striking result.

This exercise not only helped me enhance my technical proficiency but also sharpened my eye as a designer. It was a valuable experience that boosted my confidence in using 3D tools and reaffirmed my passion for blending technology with intimate fashion.

**How do you usually approach planning and preparing for a new project in CLO?**

Every CLO project starts with a clear intention—whether it’s a function, technique, or aesthetic I want to explore. From there, I create a moodboard and technical sketch to guide the process.

I begin by defining the avatar’s shape and the basic structure of the garment, either by adapting one of my sloper patterns or creating a new one from scratch. At this stage, I also design any trims or hardware if needed.

Once the base pattern is well-fitted and refined, I build the key design features and determine the most efficient construction order. I then add all sewing details, hardware, and trims.

Finally, once the garment is properly simulated, I pose the avatar and create a visual atmosphere that enhances the character of the piece and highlights its construction details.

![45b4fad37d21454999c514e32df2b387](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/01956365227a4857b5a85bc21a36c38e/images/45b4fad37d21454999c514e32df2b387SCREEN_1%20%281%29.png)

**What was your favorite part of working on this project in CLO?**

What I enjoy most about CLO is how naturally it extends my hands-on craft. My experience in sewing, pattern making, and fabric handling integrates seamlessly into the digital process.

I love that I can translate my manual skills into a digital space without compromising on precision or detail. Watching a garment come to life through simulation—and being able to adjust patterns in real time—is incredibly satisfying. It feels similar to traditional making, but with greater speed and no material waste.

I also enjoy the ability to iterate designs freely and visualize ideas that were once only in my head or sketchbook. As an independent designer, CLO allows me to test and validate new designs without the cost of physical sampling.  


![c71b45c53dd74f8f912c8950dbb2087d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/01956365227a4857b5a85bc21a36c38e/images/c71b45c53dd74f8f912c8950dbb2087dSCREEN_3%20%281%29.png)

**Which features in CLO were most useful for this project?**

Several key tools were essential to recreating this design in CLO.

First, the **Layer** function was critical. It allowed me to stack closely positioned pieces without them interfering with each other during simulation. Assigning layers correctly helped maintain a clean, realistic finish.

Another important tool was **Strengthen** , which I used during early construction stages. It kept pieces stable while I shaped them, and once I achieved the desired form, I turned it off to observe the fabric’s natural behavior.

Lastly, I relied on **Freeze** to lock delicate sections in place while working on other areas. This helped me manipulate complex parts of the design without compromising the overall structure.

Together, these tools gave me precise control and made it possible to simulate a complex, delicate garment with accuracy.

**How is 3D fashion making the industry more accessible for emerging designers?**

3D fashion is transforming the industry, especially for emerging designers like myself.

In the past, creating a collection required significant investment in materials, equipment, and production. Now, tools like CLO let designers visualize their ideas, test fit and proportions, experiment with prints, and present their work professionally—all without producing a single physical sample.

This dramatically lowers financial barriers and opens up room for creativity and experimentation. Working digitally also allows new designers to build a professional portfolio and reach a global audience, even from a modest setup.  


![d4e2cc5a849e4244967d55df0546bf31](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/01956365227a4857b5a85bc21a36c38e/images/d4e2cc5a849e4244967d55df0546bf31SCREEN_2%20%281%29.png)

**How do you differentiate yourself from other 3D fashion creators today?**

While I agree that differentiation is important, it’s not something I actively chase. I simply create from where I stand and stay true to my journey.

I’m a craftswoman at heart. My goal in 3D is to keep the spirit of sewing alive. I use CLO as an extension of my hands, infusing technical knowledge and manual sensitivity into each simulation so that my digital garments carry soul, precision, and intention.

I don’t follow trends—I draw inspiration from personal experiences and what truly moves me. I believe that true differentiation comes from being honest with your process and consistently working from that place of authenticity.

**How is 3D design helping emerging designers in Chile gain more visibility?**

In Chile, 3D design is still in the early stages, but it’s already opening up new opportunities—especially in terms of accessibility.

We’re a small market with geographic limitations, and our fashion scene is largely driven by independent designers. Tools like CLO make it possible to create and test ideas without the typical barriers of cost or material availability.

In our context—where getting certain supplies can be expensive or slow—3D helps us prototype and validate ideas quickly and accurately. It’s a powerful resource for independent creators.

![eb371047401a4436a77b42f531e70914](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/01956365227a4857b5a85bc21a36c38e/images/eb371047401a4436a77b42f531e70914BANNER.png)

**What exciting changes are you seeing in the adoption of 3D fashion in Chile and South America?**

3D fashion in South America is still emerging, but more designers are starting to incorporate it into their process.

In larger markets like Brazil, where the industry is more established, big brands and design studios are already using tools like CLO. In Chile, we’re seeing growing interest from independent designers, which is exciting.

Despite challenges like pricing, language barriers, and access to learning resources, there’s a strong sense of curiosity and motivation to explore new technologies. Given how culturally rich and creative the region is, I believe digital design can be a powerful tool for sharing our unique perspectives with the world.

title: Tack Tool - new version issue
content:

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi. Can you please add images or a screen recording so we can see what is happening

Comment 2: not like that, different

Comment 3: Hi! Is the freezed object a symmetrical pattern to the pattern you are editing?
Reply 1: hi,Sorry for the delay response .Yes it is symmetrical pattern.
Reply 2: That is the reason. When you edit symmetrical/instance pattern it will edit the freezed twin the same way. The freezing is useful for simulations, so that the good simulated pattern is not affected by simulation of a new pattern piece.
content_description: This web page aims to address and provide solutions for issues related to object instability after freezing in design or modeling software.
